text: Senate passes sweeping infrastructure bill in bipartisan vote, allocating $1.2 trillion for roads, bridges, broadband expansion, and public transit upgrades over the next decade.
Olympic sprinter breaks 100m world record at Diamond League meet in Zurich, posting a time of 9.54 seconds in ideal wind conditions before a sell-out crowd.
OpenAI releases new reasoning model claiming 40% improvement over previous generation on math and coding benchmarks, expanding context window to two million tokens.
Researchers at MIT develop self-healing polymer that repairs structural damage in minutes when exposed to sunlight, potentially revolutionizing aerospace and construction materials.
WHO declares end of mpox public health emergency of international concern, citing declining case counts across all affected regions and successful vaccine rollout.
Taylor Swift breaks record for highest-grossing concert tour in history, surpassing previous record by over $400 million as Eras Tour concludes its global leg.
Federal Reserve raises interest rates by 25 basis points citing persistent inflation, sending markets lower as analysts debate whether further hikes are imminent.
Arctic sea ice reaches second-lowest extent ever recorded for September, alarming scientists who warn the region may experience ice-free summers within fifteen years.
Premier League transfer window closes with record £2.8 billion spent, with Chelsea and Manchester City accounting for nearly half of all spending across the division.
CRISPR gene therapy trial shows complete remission in 28 of 30 sickle cell disease patients, offering hope for a permanent cure to the debilitating condition.
EU parliament votes to ban fossil fuel vehicles by 2035, with member states given flexibility on implementation timelines subject to emissions reduction benchmarks.
Nvidia announces next-generation GPU architecture claiming 3x performance improvement over current flagship, driving company valuation past three trillion dollars in after-hours trading.
State health officials report measles outbreak linked to unvaccinated community in rural Pennsylvania, urging residents to check vaccination records.
Netflix original documentary on climate migration wins Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature, drawing 45 million viewers in its opening week on the platform.
IPO of battery startup raises $3.4 billion in largest clean energy offering of the year, with founders promising to halve EV charging times using new solid-state technology.
Women's World Cup final draws 2.1 billion viewers worldwide as host nation claims first title in tournament history with a dramatic penalty shootout victory.
Congressional hearing on AI safety regulation draws testimony from leading researchers warning of existential risk, with lawmakers divided on appropriate oversight frameworks.
Amazon announces 12,000 new fulfilment center jobs alongside rollout of autonomous delivery robots in 15 US cities, sparking debate about net employment effects.
Deforestation in the Amazon basin reached 12,000 square kilometers last year, a 35% increase year-on-year driven by agricultural expansion and illegal logging.
UCLA study links ultra-processed food consumption to 42% increased risk of type 2 diabetes, calling for clearer labeling standards and school nutrition reform.
Former president indicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in connection with hush money payments made ahead of the 2016 election.
NASA's Artemis mission successfully deploys lunar surface rover capable of drilling for water ice deposits, marking humanity's first sustained lunar presence since Apollo.
Streaming wars intensify as Disney+ and Hulu merge into single platform, with combined subscriber base of 220 million challenging Netflix's global dominance.
Climate summit in Dubai produces landmark agreement committing 190 countries to tripling renewable energy capacity by 2030 and phasing out coal subsidies.
Marathon world record smashed by 47 seconds in Berlin, with Kenyan runner becoming first human to complete 26.2 miles in under two hours in a major race.
Pharmaceutical giant Merck settles opioid lawsuits for $4.85 billion, joining dozens of companies whose settlements now total over $50 billion nationwide.
Breakthrough in quantum computing: IBM achieves 1,000-qubit processor with error rates low enough for practical commercial applications in logistics and drug discovery.
Heart disease rates drop 22% over decade as statins, dietary changes, and smoking decline combine, but researchers warn obesity epidemic threatens to reverse gains.
Streaming platform Spotify reports podcasting revenue overtakes music for first time, reshaping its content investment strategy toward exclusive audio deals.
Wildfire season breaks records across five western states, with California alone losing 3.2 million acres and 15,000 structures, displacing 80,000 residents.
Chipmaker TSMC announces $40 billion Arizona fab expansion following US CHIPS Act incentives, aiming to manufacture advanced 2nm nodes domestically by 2028.
Elite ultramarathon runner wins Badwater 135 for third consecutive year, completing the 135-mile desert race in temperatures exceeding 120°F in record time.
G7 nations pledge $600 billion infrastructure fund for developing nations as alternative to Belt and Road, targeting energy, digital, and transport projects.
New study of 500,000 participants finds intermittent fasting reduces cardiovascular disease markers by 18% regardless of total caloric intake, challenging existing dietary guidelines.
Video game industry revenue reaches $350 billion globally, surpassing film and music combined, driven by mobile gaming growth in Southeast Asia and Africa.
Biotech firm IPOs at $8 billion valuation after FDA grants breakthrough therapy designation to its AI-designed cancer immunotherapy targeting previously undruggable proteins.
Landmark climate liability lawsuit brought by 16 coastal municipalities against oil majors proceeds in federal court, with potential damages exceeding $1 trillion.
Formula 1 announces expansion to three new markets in Africa and Southeast Asia, doubling the calendar to 40 races annually starting in 2027.
Privacy regulators in EU and UK open joint investigation into major social media platform's use of facial recognition for targeted advertising without explicit consent.
Pediatricians call for ban on social media for children under 16, citing new meta-analysis linking heavy use to depression, anxiety, and disrupted sleep in adolescents.
